prediction_braking compares held recorded input with an instantaneous braking box solution. What does it discriminate? It tests whether the recorded terminal input is consistent with what a braking solution would produce — i.e., whether the controller's applied terminal tension already commands braking (so residual motion is due to objective weighting truncation or plant) vs. whether the applied input is not a braking command (suggesting the plan terminated on position and never commanded braking).

H1: The recorded terminal commanded tensions at the terminal projected state already equal (within tolerance) the instantaneous braking-box solution, i.e., the controller does command braking; residual motion then is not attributable to absent braking command.
H2: The recorded terminal commanded tensions materially differ from the braking-box solution — the applied input is a position-holding plan without braking, consistent with terminal-objective weighting/horizon truncation failing to command braking.

Metrics: e.g., prediction braking tip speed at 0.01 s, terminal tip position error, delta between recorded input and braking-box tensions, tension delta in N, etc.

Acceptance criteria: e.g., the check reports the braking-box solution and the recorded-input rollout; a difference above/below a stated threshold.
